title: T19-S v2: covariance-error observables, theorem-domain check and residual orders on G1

provenance.supersedes: ../successor_20260912/t19s/PROTOCOL_T19S.json (schema mlst-successor-protocol/1, frozen 2026-09-12T00:20:00Z) together with PROTOCOL_T19S_AMENDMENT_2026-09-12.md; those files are immutable design inputs and are not edited
design_inputs: experiments/paper1/t19_coupling.py (archived T19 runner, v2 after the 11 Sep audit)
experiments/paper1/g1.py (frozen generator G1: d = 256, rank 2, N = 512)
MS plan/MLST_COMPLETENESS_AND_LOCAL_BUILD_2026-09-13.md sections 'Specific problems found in those inputs' and 'L1'
MS reviews/2026-09-12-mlst-paper-review.md findings S1 and S4
what_is_corrected: the deterministic part now implements the covariance model A(I+E)^{-1} (the paper's and the archive's); the additive model A + eps G is kept only as a labelled CONTROL and is never reported as the paper's model
'stop when acceptance decided' is replaced by a fixed confirmation allocation scored once; the pilot only freezes the eps and m values used for scoring

fit counts are derived from an enumerated run matrix (every estimator invocation on drawn data is a fit; engineered/analytic subspace solves are counted separately as solves), not from seeds x arms in prose
residual slopes are estimated ALONG A FIXED PERTURBATION DIRECTION per path (paired points), not from independently drawn directions at each eps

first-order agreement ratios have a predeclared ABSOLUTE-error branch when the first-order prediction is zero (block-diagonal and zero families): the ratio is recorded as null, never divided through, and the absolute residual is compared with the bound

the theorem-domain check is the absolute remainder bound ||P_hat - P - delta P||_op <= 44 eta^2 for eta <= 1/10 (MLST Prop 3.4); the factor-of-two first-order band on the projector Frobenius norm is a separate DESCRIPTIVE estimand and is not treated as the theorem

observables are compared like with like: the archived T19 residual is the GRAPH residual ||T - T1||_F; graph, projector-matrix (operator and Frobenius), projector-norm and principal-angle residuals each have their own predeclared order per family

the independently estimated covariance arm classifies every fit by the REALIZED eta computed from the sample spectrum; the m allocation is predeclared, every attempt is reported, and no draw is rejected to populate a domain
sample versus population coordinates are recorded explicitly for every eta, gap and basis
the expired 2026-09-12 mission allocation (120 fits) is not carried over; the budget below is computed from the enumerated matrix and measured fixture timings

question: On the frozen generator G1 (d = 256, rank 2, N = 512): (1) do the four displacement observables of the covariance-error model A(I+E)^{-1} have the predeclared leading residual orders along fixed perturbation directions, for pure-coupling and generic errors, and do the block-diagonal and zero controls leave the subspace exactly unchanged; (2) on paired synthetic fits with engineered errors (sample eigenbasis), independently estimated covariances (full sample covariance and Toeplitz, population-basis error) and training-sample error, does every fit realised inside the theorem domain (eta <= 0.1) satisfy the absolute remainder bound 44 eta^2, how well does the first-order projector norm agree descriptively, and what residual orders are measured along fixed directions?

model.paper: Sigma_hat = Sigma^{1/2}(I+E)Sigma^{1/2}; the estimator fitted with Sigma_hat returns the top-k invariant subspace of A(I+E)^{-1} in true-whitened coordinates (NOT the additive A+E)
model.first_order_graph: X1_ji = -lambda_j E_ji / (lambda_i - lambda_j), i retained, j discarded (E in the eigenbasis of A)
model.first_order_projector: delta P has off-diagonal blocks X1 and X1^T and zero diagonal blocks
model.proposition: MLST Prop 3.4: if eta = eps lambda_1 / delta <= 1/10 (eps = ||E||_op, delta = lambda_k - lambda_{k+1}) then ||P_hat - P - delta P||_op <= 44 eta^2
model.additive_control: A + eps G with first order G_ji/(lambda_i - lambda_j); a CONTROL, not the paper's model
model.model_identity_check: for every covariance-error fit the fitted subspace is compared with the deterministic top-k invariant subspace of A_hat(I+E)^{-1} (one solve); sin(theta) must be < 1e-6 (unless a floor was applied)

hypotheses: H1 (deterministic, covariance model): along a fixed direction the residual orders are generic = (graph 2, projector_matrix 2, projector_norm 2, angle 2) and pure_coupling = (3, 2, 3, 3); block-diagonal and zero E leave the subspace exactly unchanged; the 2-D example A = diag(2,1), E = eps[[0,1],[1,0]], k = 1 has graph coordinate t = -2 eps/(1 + sqrt(1 + 8 eps^2)) and ||P_hat - P - delta P||_F / eps^2 -> sqrt(2)

H2 (theorem-domain check): every confirmation fit realised at eta <= 0.1 with lambda_min(I+E) > 0 satisfies ||P_hat - P - delta P||_op <= 44 eta^2 (a necessary consistency check of Prop 3.4 on G1; passing does not prove the proposition)

H3 (descriptive): the projector Frobenius-norm displacement agrees with its first-order value sqrt(2)||X1||_F within a factor of two on in-domain fits; the stress range eta in [0.2, 1.3] is reported as outside the theorem

H4 (stress test): the residual orders of families C (pure coupling) and F (generic) measured on paired fits along fixed sample-basis directions agree with H1 within 0.3; the archived registered T19 slope prediction (one order for every observable) remains NOT MET and is not re-scored here
independent_unit: one training draw = one seed (all arms of a paired cell share the draw; the calibration pool and the direction are seed-indexed); deterministic cells have no statistical replication and are reported per direction

observables.graph: ||X - X1||_F with X = C_disc C_ret^{-1}, C = Q^T V (archived T19 observable, t19_coupling.displacement)
observables.projector_matrix: ||dP - delta P||_op (the theorem's quantity) and ||dP - delta P||_F, dP = C C^T - P0
observables.angle: || sin Theta - sigma(X1) ||_2, sin Theta = singular values of Q_disc^T V
also_recorded: pairwise gaps and delta (sample and population)
eta (sample and population; which one classifies is recorded)
eigensolver residual max_i ||M v_i - mu_i v_i||
bound violation max(0, ||R||_op - 44 eta^2) with in-domain flag
ratio measured/first-order per observable, null in the absolute branch
sin(theta) to oracle and to planted

covariance_model.block_diagonal: exact: absolute branch, displacement must be < 1e-9 at every eps; ratio null
covariance_model.zero: exact: absolute branch, displacement must be < 1e-12; ratio null

predeclared_orders.slope_window: points with eta <= 0.1 (in-domain) along one fixed direction, at least 3 points, residual above the 1e-13 numerical floor; the window is recorded per path
predeclared_orders.deterministic_slopes_are_assertions: a deterministic slope outside tolerance, a control displacement above threshold, a 2-D closed-form mismatch or an identity error above 1e-10 is a scientific-check failure: reduce exits 4 and the run is not reducible
predeclared_orders.paired_slopes_are_outcomes: paired-fit slopes outside tolerance are reported as outcomes (H4 not met), never as a failure of the package

production.generator: g1_d256 (experiments/paper1/g1.py; recorded cond 32.0, lambda_1 19.44, Delta_lambda 5.20 re-checked at run time)

deterministic.direction_seeds: 20260913 + index; a direction is a design constant, not a replicate

paired.arms: per seed: oracle (Sigma, N) ; C and F at every eps of eps_grid with ONE direction per (seed, family) built in the sample eigenbasis ; S_full and S_toeplitz at every m ; D at every N of the ratio grid except the oracle N
paired.joint_arm: not retained: joint E x D sensitivity is not an estimand of this package; the engineered and estimated arms are paired against the oracle on the same draw (D held fixed), the D arm has E = 0

fixture.generator: g1_like_d32 (same PSD shape with f_knee = 4/d, rank, SNR, basis seed; NOT G1)

deterministic.operator: analytic operator: lambda = (20, 6, 1 x 30) in a random orthogonal basis (seed 20260913); lambda_1/delta = 4, close to G1's 3.74

classification.eta_definition: eta = ||E||_op * lambda_1 / (lambda_k - lambda_{k+1}) computed from the SAMPLE spectrum of A_hat for engineered and estimated arms (the fit diagonalises A_hat, so A_hat is the operator the proposition is applied to); eta_D uses the population spectrum for the training-sample arm

classes.stress: 0.2 <= eta <= 1.3 (the range the archived T19 tested; OUTSIDE the theorem)

classification.rule: classification is by the REALIZED eta of each fit; every attempt is reported with its class; nothing is redrawn or dropped to populate a class

pilot_selection_rule.written_by: the pilot reducer (reduce --allow-partial after the pilot cells) into <RUN_ROOT>/PILOT_SELECTION.json; a confirmation cell refuses to start unless that file exists and records its sha256; the confirmation reducer refuses if any confirmation cell saw a different selection
pilot_selection_rule.engineered: eps_in_domain = the three largest eps of eps_grid whose median realised eta_sample over pilot seeds is <= 0.1; eps_stress = the smallest and the largest eps whose median eta_sample lies in [0.2, 1.3]
pilot_selection_rule.estimated: per estimator (S_full, S_toeplitz): m_in_domain = every m whose median realised eta_sample is <= 0.1 (may be empty; then the theorem-domain estimand is reported as undefined for that estimator with the median eta at the largest m); m_stress = every m whose median eta_sample lies in [0.2, 1.3]
pilot_selection_rule.scored_fits: estimand (a) uses confirmation fits in selected in-domain arms that are ALSO realised in-domain; selected-arm fits that fell outside the domain are counted and listed, not dropped silently; estimands (b) and (c) are reported for every class with the class label
pilot_selection_rule.confirmation_allocation: confirmation cells run the SAME fixed grid as the pilot (every eps, m and N); selection only decides which arms are scored; every arm is reported

estimands.a_theorem_domain_check: fraction of realised in-domain confirmation fits (engineered C, F; estimated S_full, S_toeplitz) with bound violation == 0, per source and pooled; per-seed fractions bootstrapped across seeds (2000 replicates, fixed seed)
estimands.b_first_order_agreement_norm: fraction of fits whose ratio ||dP||_F / (sqrt(2)||X1||_F) lies in [0.5, 2], per source and class; descriptive; not the theorem
estimands.c_residual_orders: per family C and F, per observable: per-seed log-log slope along the fixed sample-basis direction over the selected in-domain eps (>= 3 points, else over the full path and labelled), mean across seeds with bootstrap CI, compared with the predeclared order within 0.3; an outcome, not an assertion
estimands.d_training_sample_arm: descriptive: graph/projector/norm/angle first-order agreement and eta_D by N (additive perturbation; the 44 eta^2 bound is not asserted for D)

controls: zero perturbation: exact identity (displacement < 1e-12), absolute branch
block-diagonal E: subspace unchanged (displacement < 1e-9), absolute branch
2-D closed-form example: graph t = -2 eps/(1 + sqrt(1 + 8 eps^2)) to 1e-12; ||P_hat - P - delta P||_F/eps^2 = 1.414143, 1.414196, 1.414209 at eps = 0.01, 0.005, 0.0025 to 1e-5
exact projector identity ||dP||_F^2 = 2 tr[S(I+S)^{-1}] to 1e-10 at every point
additive model A + eps G: labelled control, orders reported separately, never the paper's model
model identity: fitted subspace equals the invariant subspace of A_hat(I+E)^{-1} to sin(theta) < 1e-6
oracle fit: zero graph displacement in the sample eigenbasis (< 1e-8)

bootstrap.type: percentile bootstrap of the mean across seeds

inference.multiplicity: orders are predeclared per (family, observable); estimands (a)-(d) are reported jointly with no selection among observables after seeing outcomes
inference.development_outputs: never citable; the fixture reducer runs the same code on development cells and labels everything development_only

stopping_rule: fixed allocation: 20 pilot cells (seeds 1000-1019) then 100 confirmation cells (seeds 2000-2099), every arm of the fixed grid in every cell (32 fits per cell), plus 16 deterministic cells; scored once after all confirmation cells are complete; no outcome-dependent stopping, no extension, no early stop

failure_interpretation.H1_fails: a deterministic check failure is a code or derivation defect: reduce exits 4; nothing is reported as an outcome until it is fixed in a new protocol version
failure_interpretation.H2_fails: report the violating fits by (source, family, eps or m, eta, lambda_min, remainder/eta^2); do not adjust eps, m or the classification to recover; a violation inside eta <= 0.1 is evidence against the stated constant on G1 and is reported as such
failure_interpretation.H3_fails: descriptive; report the ratio distribution by class
failure_interpretation.H4_fails: report the measured slopes with CIs; the registered T19 prediction stays NOT MET regardless
failure_interpretation.estimated_arm_never_in_domain: if no m reaches eta <= 0.1 for an estimator, report the realised eta by m and state that the theorem domain is not reachable at the allocated m for that estimator; this is a finding, not a reason to enlarge m after the fact

budget.solves_planned_from_matrix: reported by enumerate (deterministic points + sample-operator and model-identity solves)
budget.scale_basis: measured locally on 2 cores (13 Sep 2026, numpy 2.4.4): one paired cell at d = 256, N = 512, m <= 2048 d took 6.5-7.8 s warm (one cold outlier 15.8 s; 32 fits; the m = 2048 d calibration stream of 134M normals dominates) against 0.036-0.048 s for one fixture paired cell (d = 32, N = 96, 15 fits): ratio 140-200, declared 200; one deterministic cell on the d = 256 G1 operator took 0.5-0.7 s against 0.007-0.017 s at d = 32: ratio 40-100, declared 100; peak memory per worker about 0.3 GB because the calibration pool is streamed in 8192-row chunks; the production point estimate is therefore about 120 x 8 s + 16 x 1 s = 17 CPU-minutes before retries
budget.retry_policy: a failed cell may be retried at most twice; each attempt is charged at start; charged + planned above the cap refuses the attempt (exit 2); the 960-fit headroom covers 30 paired-cell retries
budget.replicates: bootstrap replicates are reported separately and are not fits

explicitly_not_claimed: a finite-perturbation theorem or any extension of the 44 eta^2 bound beyond eta <= 0.1
that the stress range eta in [0.2, 1.3] validates or extends the proposition
that passing the theorem-domain check proves Prop 3.4 (it is a necessary consistency check on one generator)
that a deployment surrogate for E (which needs the true covariance) has been validated: the engineered arms demonstrate a mechanism under a known reference covariance (review finding S4)
that the archived registered T19 slope prediction is met: it remains NOT MET; this package explains why one order per observable was a category error and does not re-score it
